{{Short description|Polish mathematician, philosopher (1913–1992)}}
'''Franciszek Indan Pykna''' (12 July 1913 – 29 January 1992) was a [[Polish people|Polish]] mathematician, philosopher, and linguist.

== Early life ==
Pykna was born in [[Riga]], [[Russian Empire]], to Polish parents Kazimierz Indan Pykno and Benigna Norwillo. He spent his early childhood travelling with his parents through Russia; they returned to Poland ([[Kunow]] and Odrowaz). They finally settled in [[Kovel]], where he went to Juliusz Slowacki High School. After graduating he moved to [[Vilnius]] in order to study at [[Vilnius University]].

== Academic work ==
Pykna achieved a master's degree in 1937 with his thesis "The concept of ethical philosophy of Descartes".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.elv-akt.net/ressources/archives.php?id_catalogue=19&ordre=title&option=asc |title=e-ARCHIVES &#124; Archiwum Kazimierza Twardowskiego |publisher=Elv-akt.net |date=2008-09-23 |accessdate=2012-01-15}}</ref> He became an assistant in the Philosophy department of Stefan Batory University while working on his PhD in the subject of ethics<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.elv-akt.net/informations/actualites.php?id_actualite=19&langue=pl |title=AKTUALNOŚCI &#124; Archiwum Kazimierza Twardowskiego |publisher=Elv-akt.net |date=2008-08-12 |accessdate=2012-01-15}}</ref> He was nominated as senior assistant to the department of Philosophy starting on 1 September 1939,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.elv-akt.net/ressources/archives.php?id_archive=231 |title=e-ARCHIVES &#124; Archiwum Kazimierza Twardowskiego |publisher=Elv-akt.net |date=2008-09-23 |accessdate=2012-01-15}}</ref> which was the day [[World War II]] started; the university was evacuated to Poland. After the war, most of the staff settled in [[Toruń]], Poland, creating [[Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń]]. In 1945 he worked in the department of logic studies at the university as a senior assistant to professor Tadeusz Czezowski. Between 1947 and 1948 he headed the mathematical department in the Fourth College in Torun.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.loiv.torun.pl/?q=node/144 |title=Byli nauczyciele &#124; IV LO im. Tadeusza Kościuszki w Toruniu |publisher=Loiv.torun.pl |date= |accessdate=2012-01-15}}</ref>

He then returned to Nicolaus Copernicus University, working with professor [[Roman Ingarden]] and Tadeusz Czezowski. He started publishing his works: "Revue Philosophique de la France et de l'Etranger", "Pozytywizm etyczny Emila Durkheima" ([[Emile Durkheim]]'s ethical positivism; 1960),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://durkheim.uchicago.edu/Bibliography/Bib03.html |title=A Bibliography of Works about Durkheim |publisher=Durkheim.uchicago.edu |date= |accessdate=2012-01-15}}</ref> "Set of tasks of probability and mathematical statistics" (1962)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://150.254.171.193/ipac20/ipac.jsp?session=1E73DH1187659.747638&profile=bgpp&page=2&group=0&term=Rachunek+prawdopodobie%C5%84stwa+--+zadania+i+%C4%87wiczenia.&index=SW&uindex=&aspect=subtab14&menu=search&ri=1&source=~!bpp&1273951188119#focus |title=Horizon Information Portal |publisher=150.254.171.193 |date=2011-09-26 |accessdate=2012-01-15}}</ref> "Cohorts method applied to arrays of elimination" (1967), and "Mathematics Theory and a set of tasks" (1973).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://allegro.pl/item1152101372_matematyka_teoria_i_zbior_zadan_indan.html#gallery|title = Matematyka Teoria i zbiór zadań / Indan - 1152101372 - oficjalne archiwum Allegro}}</ref>

His correspondence with Tadeusz Kotarbinski (philosopher and professor of [[University of Warsaw]]) can be found in the archives of Archives of Janina and Tadeusz Kotarbinski, 1962.<ref>[http://www.ifispan.waw.pl/files/bibfis/data/data/zbiory_2/Archiwalia%20Janiny%20i%20Tadeusza%20Kotarbinskich%20%20cz.1.pdf]{{dead link|date=January 2012}}</ref> Franciszek Indan was a board member of the Polish Society of Mathematics from 1971 to 1981.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ptm.org.pl/historia/wladzeptm/ |accessdate=August 3, 2010 |url-status=dead |title=Władze PTM w latach 1919-2010|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110107081646/http://www.ptm.org.pl/historia/wladzeptm/ |archivedate=January 7, 2011 }}</ref> His works are available on line from Twardowski Digital Archives.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.elv-akt.net/informations/actualites.php?id_actualite=19&langue=en |title=NEWS &#124; Archiwum Kazimierza Twardowskiego |publisher=Elv-akt.net |date= |accessdate=2012-01-15}}</ref>

== Private life ==
He was married to Zofia Siemaszko, with whom he had five children.
